issues.legal_issue: Sections 73 and 74 of the Indian Contract Act do not apply to forfeiture of an earnest-money deposit under Rule 9(5) of the SARFAESI Rules.

Rule 9(5) of the SARFAESI Rules requires forfeiture of the prescribed earnest-money deposit upon the successful auction purchaser’s default, irrespective of the loss suffered by the secured creditor or the debt recovered.
Forfeiture under Rule 9(5) of the SARFAESI Rules does not constitute unjust enrichment merely because the secured creditor later recovers its dues or sells the secured asset for a higher price.
Rule 9(5) of the SARFAESI Rules cannot be read down merely because its prescribed forfeiture may have a harsh effect.
A court may set aside forfeiture under Rule 9(5) only in very rare and exceptional circumstances, which were not established in this case.
